title: Hill-based reformulation of the Hodgkin-Huxley model for mapping gating changes to neuronal excitability
task: Map ion-channel gating mutations to neuronal excitability using Hill-based Hodgkin-Huxley reformulation
key_results: Hill formulation captures qualitative excitability increase from Nav1.7 mutations (A863P, F1449V, A1632G) but overestimates threshold reduction magnitude; provides explicit parameter mapping from steady-state voltage shifts without full kinetic data
comments: The framework trades quantitative accuracy for reproducibility when kinetic constraints are unavailable, but mutation-specific predictions still require additional cellular context.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hill formulation can map reported activation descriptors to model parameters with explicit parameter relations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Hill approach provides reproducible mapping superior to refitting classical HH, though both require kinetic assumptions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nav1.7 mutations increase neuronal excitability via conductance changes
hypotheses.result: Qualitatively confirmed but quantitative magnitude overestimated in Hill model

title: Quantitative label-free characterization of nanoparticles and subcellular structures in live cells using confocal scattering microscopy
task: Enable quantitative label-free characterization of nanoparticles and subcellular structures in live cells using confocal scattering microscopy
key_results: C-SCAT signal from nanoparticles remains comparable across cellular volume to first-order approximation; effective polarizability of actin filaments, ER, and mitochondria measurable; basal nuclear envelope dynamics quantified
comments: The framework successfully decouples particle properties from intracellular background variation, enabling multiparametric analysis, though model-dependent polarizability estimates introduce systematic dependencies.

hypotheses.hypothesis: C-SCAT signal reflects particle polarizability change across varying background amplitudes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in buffers and cell-like conditions; signal proportional to expected polarizability changes

hypotheses.hypothesis: C-SCAT signal from nanoparticles is comparable across cellular volume
hypotheses.result: Confirmed to first-order approximation, enabling robust volume-independent measurements

title: IL-22–mediated antioxidant signaling preserves intestinal epithelial integrity under high-salt dietary stress
task: Elucidate how IL-22 protects intestinal epithelium from high-salt diet-induced oxidative stress and barrier dysfunction
key_results: IL-22 activates STAT3-dependent antioxidant program (Gclc, Sod2) limiting mitochondrial superoxide; IL-22−/− mice exhibited severe injury (colon shortening, barrier leakage, weight loss); recombinant IL-22 restored barrier integrity STAT3-dependently
comments: Elegant dissection of epithelial resilience mechanisms using loss/gain-of-function models; dysbiosis shown as insufficient for injury, highlighting direct epithelial signaling as primary protective mechanism.

hypotheses.hypothesis: IL-22 protects epithelium from HSD via STAT3-dependent antioxidant signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: IL-22 induced Gclc and Sod2; recombinant IL-22 restored barrier integrity STAT3-dependently

hypotheses.hypothesis: HSD increases epithelial oxidative stress through NOX1/4
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: HSD elevated Nox1/4 and epithelial oxidative stress; NOX1/4 inhibition restored functional gene expression

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dysbiosis is primary driver of HSD-induced injury in IL-22−/− mice
hypotheses.result: Refuted: Antibiotic depletion and germ-free transfer showed dysbiosis insufficient for severe injury

title: A cue-locality audit framework for attributing spurious temporal shortcuts in deep sequence models

GRU trained via empirical risk minimization (ERM)

task: 3D reconstruction of complex disaster scenes using frequency-aware and depth-guided neural radiance fields
key_results: PSNR improvement of 1.865 dB over baseline; depth MSE reduced by 88.99% vs. depth-prior-only model
comments: Strong empirical gains on synthetic disasters but generalization to real catastrophe scenes and computational efficiency on edge devices remain unaddressed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Frequency-aware gating + depth priors mitigate geometric floaters and blur in sparse-view disaster reconstruction

title: Enhancing the performance of multi-access edge computing based intelligent transportation system
task: Multi-access edge computing optimization for vehicle-based intelligent transportation systems
key_results: Best-Score Server Selection Algorithm (BSSSA) with Least Recently Used cache policy increases packet delivery ratio, reduces latency and energy consumption, improves cache hit ratios via centralized SDN management
comments: Practical MEC+ITS integration using OMNeT++ and Simu5G simulation; however, purely simulation-based evaluation without real vehicular deployment, and lack of quantitative performance metrics (PDR, latency, energy) reported in abstract limits verifiability.

title: Multi-horizon wind speed prediction with physics-embedded state space neural operator learning
task: Multi-horizon wind-speed forecasting with physics-embedded state space operator learning
key_results: PESO-Net: MAE 2.080 m/s, RMSE 2.622 m/s, R² 0.176, 95.56% empirical coverage, interval score 12.048; comparable to PatchTST (RMSE 2.727 m/s); predicted shear exponents 0.229–0.235 vs. observed ~0.222 (correlations 0.287–0.302)
comments: Well-calibrated prediction intervals and comprehensive baseline comparisons appreciated; limited physical agreement on shear exponents, non-significant paired bootstrap contrast with Transformer, and prior-test-set leakage substantially weaken claims of superiority.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis and machine learning prediction of road traffic crash hotspots: a case of Amhara region, Ethiopia

title: AlphaDiffract: automated crystallographic analysis of powder X-ray diffraction data

title: Low-frequency noise reduction in laser-induced graphene devices by noble metal nanoparticles decoration
task: Reduce low-frequency noise in laser-induced graphene devices
key_results: Au-decorated LIG achieved 32-times reduction in normalized voltage noise; noise reduction order: Pt < Ag < Au

title: Theoretical study on the in-plane vertical and rotational coupled vibration of a shield cutter head

comments: Multi-scale perturbation method yields clean analytical predictions, but experimental validation on actual cutter heads is absent; assumptions of linear coupling and harmonic excitation may not hold under dynamic face pressure variation.

Two-degree-of-freedom mass-spring-damper system with coupling stiffness

title: Application of Raman spectroscopy to the first actual fuel debris retrieved from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 2
task: Characterize chemical states and oxidative products in Fukushima Daiichi Unit 2 fuel debris via Raman spectroscopy
key_results: Identified tetragonal ZrO₂, spinel-type oxides (stainless steel), and cubic (U, Zr)O₂ solid solution in retrieved debris; spectra differ significantly from previous uranium-containing particles from torus water
comments: Raman spectroscopy provides rapid, minimal-preparation characterization suitable for nuclear decommissioning, but spatial heterogeneity of fuel debris suggests multiple sampling campaigns needed for comprehensive chemical mapping.

inputs: powdered Fukushima FDNPS Unit 2 fuel debris

hypotheses.hypothesis: Raman spectroscopy can identify oxidative products and chemical phases in nuclear fuel debris with minimal sample preparation
hypotheses.result: Successfully identified ZrO₂, spinel, and (U, Zr)O₂ phases; spectra differ from previous uranium particles, indicating compositional complexity requiring further sampling
